user.description: Coin-op records what each print of your 3D printers costs. After setup, add each printer as a Device.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Coin-op is already set up. Add more printers as Devices to the existing entry.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Device
reconfigure.description: Pick a section to change. Nothing is saved until you choose Save. Changes apply to an open Run at once; a new consumption source applies from the next Run. Ended Runs never change. Detect again walks status, job and images pre-filled from the printer integration's Integration Profile, e.g. after an update renamed its entities; consumption source and price stay as they are.

user.title: Add Device
user.description: What kind of Device should Coin-op record Runs of? The Device Type decides the next steps and can't be changed later.

device.title: Home Assistant device
device.description: Pick the Device's Home Assistant device to take over its name, or leave it empty. For an integration Coin-op knows (3D printers: Anycubic 3D Printer - Local Control, Anycubic Cloud & LAN), the next steps come pre-filled from its entities; check and change them as you like.

data_description.device: Coin-op's own device for this Device is linked to it. Entity pickers in the next steps still offer every entity.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the Device. You can rename it later on its Home Assistant device page.

status.title: Status
status.description: Pick the entity that reports the Device's status. It does not need to be available now.

data_description.attribute: Read this attribute instead of the entity's state.

mapping.title: Status mapping
mapping.description: Assign each status value to what it means for a Run. A Run starts at the first running value and ends at the first finished, cancelled or ended value. Type in values that are not offered.

data_description.ended: Ends the Run with Outcome Unknown, e.g. when the printer only reports printing / not printing.

job.title: Job & Material
job.description: Optionally pick the entity that reports the name of the current print job, and the one that reports how much material the job used. A Run is named after its job, and a print that starts again with the same job name, e.g. after a power loss, continues the same Run.

data_description.entity_id: Without a job name, a print that starts again while a Run is open always continues that Run.
data_description.attribute: Read this attribute instead of the entity's state, e.g. the file name attribute of a print event entity.
data_description.material_entity_id: The printer's measured total for the job, as a length (e.g. mm of filament) or a mass (g). A length is converted to grams through the Material's diameter and density. Without it, each Run gets a Material Line Item with an empty quantity to fill in.
data_description.material_attribute: Read this attribute instead of the entity's state, e.g. the length attribute of a filament sensor.
data_description.slots: One entity per Slot of a multi-material unit, in Slot order: the first is Slot 1. Each reports the type of the Material loaded in it (e.g. PLA) as its state.
data_description.colour_attribute: The attribute of the Slot entities that carries the Material's colour as a hex code, e.g. color_hex.
data_description.loaded_slot: Reports the number of the Slot printing right now; any other value means no Slot. Each Slot loaded during a Run is matched to a Material by type and colour.

material_unit.title: Unit of the Material used attribute
material_unit.description: In which unit does the attribute report the material used? It must be a length or a mass.

images.title: Images
images.description: Optionally pick where a Run's images come from. The Thumbnail is copied while the Run is open; the camera takes the Snapshot when the Run ends. Images are stored downscaled and without metadata.

data.snapshot: Take a Snapshot when a Run ends

data_description.thumbnail: The image entity of the printer integration that shows the model being printed.
data_description.snapshot: Only with a camera. Up to three attempts; none when the end of a Run is only noticed later, e.g. after an outage.

consumption.title: Electricity consumption
consumption.description: How should Coin-op determine the electricity a Run uses?

energy.title: Energy meter
energy.description: Pick the entity that counts the Device's energy, e.g. the energy sensor of a power-measuring plug. It does not need to be available now.

data_description.attribute: Read this attribute instead of the entity's state.
data_description.factor: Multiply each reading by this to get kWh.

power.title: Power sensor
power.description: Pick the entity that reports the Device's power draw. Coin-op integrates it over time. It does not need to be available now.

data_description.attribute: Read this attribute instead of the entity's state.
data_description.running_power: Fills gaps while the sensor reports nothing. Leave empty to hold its last value.
data_description.factor: Multiply each reading by this to get W.

energy_unit.title: Unit of the energy attribute
energy_unit.description: In which unit does the attribute count energy?

data_description.factor: Multiply each reading by this to get kWh.

power_unit.title: Unit of the power attribute
power_unit.description: In which unit does the attribute report power?

data_description.factor: Multiply each reading by this to get W.

data_description.running_power: The average draw over a whole print, typically 80–150 W for a desktop FDM printer with a heated bed. Do not enter the rated power from the label or power supply: it is far higher than the real average.
data_description.paused_power: Draw while paused. Leave empty to use the running power.

price.title: Electricity price
price.description: Do you pay a fixed price per kWh, or does an entity report the current price, e.g. for a dynamic tariff?

data_description.price: What you pay per kWh, in {currency}.

price_entity.title: Price entity
price_entity.description: Pick the entity that reports the current price per kWh or MWh, in {currency} or a sub-unit like ct. Each kWh of a Run is charged at the price that applied when it was used. It does not need to be available now.

data_description.attribute: Read this attribute instead of the entity's state.
data_description.factor: Multiply each price by this to get {currency}/kWh.

price_unit.title: Unit of the price attribute
price_unit.description: In which unit does the attribute report the price?

data_description.factor: Multiply each price by this to get {currency}/kWh.

error.no_running_value: Map at least one value to running, otherwise Runs never start.
error.no_ending_value: Map at least one value to finished, cancelled or ended, otherwise Runs never end.
error.value_mapped_twice: Each value can be mapped to one target only.
error.unknown_unit: Coin-op does not recognise this unit. Enter a conversion factor, or pick another entity.
error.status_already_used: Another Device already uses this entity as its print status. Each print would be recorded twice.
error.not_length_or_mass: Coin-op can only use a length (e.g. mm) or a mass (e.g. g) as Material used. Pick another entity or unit.

data_description.spoolman_url: Optional. The address of your Spoolman server, e.g. http://192.168.1.20:7912. Materials linked to a Spoolman Filament take their price per gram from it. Leave empty to stop reading Spoolman: linked Materials keep the last price read.
data_description.markup: The Markup a new Cost Statement starts with: a percentage added on top of its subtotal. You can change it for each export.

error.cannot_connect: No Spoolman answered at this URL. Check the address and that Spoolman is running.

data_missing.message: Coin-op's stored data is missing ({stores}), probably because the file was corrupt. Coin-op did not start so it cannot overwrite your history. Open the repair issue to restore a backup or start fresh.

data_too_new.message: {store} was written by a newer version of Coin-op. Update Coin-op or restore a backup made with this version.

data_corrupt.message: Coin-op's stored data in {store} is corrupt. Coin-op did not start so it cannot overwrite your history. Restore a backup made before the damage.

init.title: Coin-op's stored data is missing
init.description:
Coin-op could not read {stores}, probably because the file was corrupt; Home Assistant kept a copy ending in `.corrupt`. Coin-op did not start so it cannot overwrite your history.

Restore a backup to get the data back, or start fresh with that data empty.

fresh_start.title: Start fresh
fresh_start.description: Coin-op starts with {stores} empty. What it held is lost unless you restore a backup later; all other Coin-op data is kept.

abort.restore: Restore a backup from before the data went missing under Settings > System > Backups. Restoring brings back all of Coin-op's data as it was then. Until then Coin-op stays stopped.

data_corrupt.title: Coin-op's stored data is corrupt
data_corrupt.description:
Coin-op could read {store}, but its content is not what Coin-op writes, e.g. after it was edited by hand. Coin-op did not start so it cannot overwrite your history.

Restore a backup made before the damage under Settings > System > Backups, or put back a copy of the file you kept. Until then Coin-op stays stopped.
